?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:5018
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2923 of 2015

Revisionist :- Kamta Prasad
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Revisionist :- Ashish Pandey,Satya Prakash Rathor
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.
Sri Rafiq Ahmad Khan, Advocate, has filed his vakalatnama in Court today, the same is taken on record.

2. This is criminal revision has been filed by the revisionist challenging the order dated 12.06.2012 passed by C.J.M. Mahoba, whereby the accused Kamta Prasad was convicted and sentenced to six months of rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1000/- and further the order passed by the appellate court in Criminal Appeal No. 71 of 2012 (Kamta Prasad Vs. State) by which the judgment and order passed by the trial court was confirmed and the appeal was dismissed.
3. During the course of arguments, the revisionist seeks to confine his contentions on the point of sentence only and has dropped the challenge on the point of conviction.
It is pointed out that the accused is in custody in this case since 21.11.2023 in consequence of execution of warrants issued against him by this Court.

sentences.text:
It is contended by the revisionist that as per prosecution version, the sample of milk was found to have milk-fats and milk solids-non-fat contents below the prescribed level and that though,
technically the matter comes within the definition provided for adulteration of food under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, however, no adulterant of the nature injurious to health,
was found in the sample.
It is argued that the only allegation is that milk-fat and milk solids-non-fat were found 16% and 29% respectively, less then the prescribed minimum standards.

It is said that this deficiency can be caused if a cattle is not fed with sufficient nutritious fodder and and there is a probability that this deficiency is attributable to the mixing of water with milk.
Next contention is that the incident occurred in the year 2007 and since then, he was not found involved in any other offence, much less the offence of food adulteration.
The accused is a farmer by profession and has been selling milk for earning some extra money.
As the matter has become quite old, hence a lenient view as regard period of sentence should be taken.
5. Learned A.G.A. submits that the matter comes within the first proviso to section 16 which provides for punishments.

The proviso to Section 16 says that the Court for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment award a sentence of imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less then Rs. 500/-, therefore, he cannot be punished for any period of sentence below three months.
6.
I went through all the material on record, this is a case where the accused was found to have been selling milk which was found marginally less in milk solids-fat and milk solids-non-fat.
This is not a case where he was found selling any milk mixed with some adulterant which could prove injurious to health of a human being.

Coupled with the above fact, this fact is also noticeable that the matter relates to an incident which happened in 2007 and since then, 16 years have passed.
7.
In the circumstances as above, I find it fit case to reduce the period of imprisonment to three months while not interfering with the amount of fine.
Accordingly, only to that extent the sentence order is modified.

8. In terms of above, this criminal revision is finally disposed of.
9.
Let a copy of the order be immediately transmitted to the court concerned for necessary action.

Order Date :- 10.1.2024 Sumit Kumar  Kamta Prasad vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194240482/
